title: Bodega Bay waves cut six-hour high-wave crossing Brier score at Monterey by 18.7% in retained 2010-2023 tests
abstract: We tested whether recent Bodega Bay wave heights improve the probability of a high-wave threshold crossing at Monterey. We reused fixed NDBC annual files and fitted logistic models on earlier years only. In 2010-2023, the main test had 316 crossings in 12,177 cases with current local wave height below the training-only 90th percentile. Adding three partner wave blocks reduced Brier score from 0.017355 to 0.014116, a gain of 18.66%. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were 13.86% to 23.37%. A six-hour partner delay gave a gain of 0.02%, with limits of -0.68% to 0.62%. The main reverse forecast gave no clear gain. Log score, a stronger penalty and a 95th-percentile check retained positive Monterey gains. This extends prior mean-error tests to crossing probabilities on overlapping data. It does not identify wave travel or establish operational warning value. One station pair, revised data, incomplete records, block crossings within storms, model choice and conditional uncertainty limit use. Code, aggregate evidence, fitted parameters, source hashes, figures and a separate solver audit support reproduction. Source records remain external.
